towns.name: 30A (Santa Rosa Beach)
towns.price: About $915K median across Santa Rosa Beach (Redfin, Aug 2026). Homes close to the beach run much higher
towns.airport: Northwest Florida Beaches (ECP) or Destin Fort Walton (VPS)
towns.watch: Peak season traffic, HOA rules, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: Sugar white sand, rare coastal dune lakes and small beach towns strung along Scenic Highway 30A.
towns.day: You bike the Timpoochee Trail for coffee in Seaside, paddle a dune lake before the wind picks up, and end the day on the sand at Grayton Beach.
todo: The New Urbanist town where The Truman Show was filmed, with a walkable town center and food trucks.
2,220 acres of beach, nature trails and coastal dune lakes.
Rare brackish lakes that sometimes open to the Gulf. Great for paddleboarding.
A paved path linking the 30A communities for biking, running and walking.
pros: Some of the best beaches in the country
cons: Heavy tourist traffic in peak season

towns.name: Destin
towns.watch: Summer crowds, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A harbor town built around fishing charters and emerald water.
towns.day: You're on a charter boat out of the harbor at dawn and back at a dockside table by lunch.
todo: Charter fishing, boardwalk dining and sunset cruises.

towns.name: Panama City Beach
towns.watch: Spring break crowds, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: Big beaches, big energy and a lot going on after dark.
towns.day: You spend the day on wide white sand and the evening at a live music spot near the pier.
todo: Jetties, clear water and a quiet side of town.

towns.name: Apalachicola
towns.price: About $300K to $385K, depending on the source (Zillow and Redfin, Aug 2026)
towns.watch: Storm surge and flooding in low areas
towns.blurb: An oyster town with brick storefronts, shrimp boats and no hurry at all.
towns.day: You walk to breakfast past the shrimp boats, browse the old brick downtown and watch the sun set over the bay.
todo: Brick storefronts from the town's cotton and oyster days.
A quiet barrier island beach just across the bridge.
cons: Far from big airports and hospitals

towns.name: Cedar Key
towns.watch: Hit hard by recent hurricanes; check rebuilding and flood zones. The nearest full grocery store is about 40 minutes away
towns.blurb: A tiny island town of clam farms, kayaks and sunsets over the Gulf.
towns.day: You kayak the backwater keys in the morning and eat clams on the dock at sunset.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Dunedin
towns.watch: Storm surge near the water
towns.blurb: A walkable, laid back downtown near some of the Gulf's best island beaches.
towns.day: You walk downtown for coffee, take the ferry to Caladesi Island for the beach, and bike the Pinellas Trail home.
todo: A barrier island beach reached by ferry.
A long paved trail running right through downtown.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Clearwater Beach
towns.watch: Visitor crowds, storm surge
towns.blurb: Soft white sand, a walkable beach strip and nightly sunset gatherings at Pier 60.
towns.day: You walk the beach at sunrise and join the crowd at Pier 60 for the sunset.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Gulfport
towns.watch: Flooding in low lying streets. Hit hard by Helene in 2024
towns.blurb: An artsy little waterfront town with a slow pace and a friendly main street.
towns.day: You wander the galleries on Beach Boulevard and catch live music by the water.
todo: Galleries and cafes leading down to the waterfront. The historic Casino Ballroom is closed for storm repairs.
pros: Small town feel near a big city
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Anna Maria Island
towns.watch: Island flooding and storm exposure
towns.blurb: Old Florida on a small island, with no high rises and a free trolley.
towns.day: You ride the trolley to breakfast, read on a quiet beach and watch the sun drop into the Gulf.
todo: Runs the length of the island.

towns.name: Longboat Key
towns.watch: Storm surge on the key
towns.blurb: A quiet, polished barrier island minutes from Sarasota's arts scene.
towns.day: You walk an uncrowded beach in the morning and head to a Sarasota show at night.
todo: Shops and dining just off the key.

towns.name: Captiva Island
towns.watch: Hit hard by Ian in 2022. Most of the village has reopened. Check flood zones
towns.blurb: A small, lush island known for shelling, sunsets and slowing down.
towns.day: You shell at low tide, bike under the banyan trees and watch the sunset from the beach.
todo: Some of the best shelling in the country, with neighboring Sanibel.
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Matlacha
towns.watch: Storm damage history; check flood zones
towns.blurb: A colorful fishing village of galleries, bait shops and bridges.
towns.day: You fish off the bridge in the morning and browse brightly painted galleries in the afternoon.
todo: Kayaking and fishing through the mangroves.
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Naples
towns.aka: Naples Beach Park Shore Vanderbilt Beach Clam Pass
towns.watch: Storm surge (Ian in 2022), summer heat
towns.blurb: Polished and peaceful, with golf, boating, a walkable downtown and calm Gulf beaches from the pier north to Vanderbilt Beach.
towns.day: You play a morning round, walk Fifth Avenue South for lunch and watch the sunset from the beach at the end of the street.
todo: The classic sunset spot. The pier is closed for a rebuild, expected to finish around mid 2027.
A mile of natural beach that often lands on best beach lists.
towns.area_name: Naples, Marco Island and the Everglades

towns.name: Key West
towns.watch: Long evacuation route, high insurance, small lots
towns.blurb: The end of the road: bikes, sunsets, live music and island time.
towns.day: You bike to coffee, spend the afternoon on the water and walk to Mallory Square for the sunset.
pros: One of a kind walkable island

towns.name: Islamorada
towns.watch: Evacuation distance, high insurance
towns.blurb: The sport fishing capital of the Keys, laid back and on the water.
towns.day: You're out on the flats at sunrise and at a waterfront fish house by sunset.
todo: World famous fishing for bonefish and tarpon.

towns.name: Miami (South Beach)
towns.watch: Flooding, traffic, high insurance
towns.blurb: Art deco, ocean views and a city that never slows down.
towns.day: You run the beachwalk at sunrise, work from a cafe and head out to dinner late.
pros: Big city energy on the beach

towns.name: Fort Lauderdale
towns.watch: Flooding, high insurance
towns.blurb: A boating city of canals, marinas and a lively beach.
towns.day: You take the boat out through the canals, then grab dinner on Las Olas.
todo: Dining and shops near the river.

towns.name: Delray Beach
towns.airport: Palm Beach airport or Fort Lauderdale (FLL)
towns.watch: Traffic, higher insurance
towns.blurb: A walkable downtown that runs right to the ocean and stays up late.
towns.day: You walk Atlantic Avenue for breakfast, hit the beach at the end of the street and come back for dinner and music.
todo: Restaurants and nightlife that run to the beach.

towns.name: Jupiter
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: Clear inlet water, a red lighthouse and a relaxed, outdoorsy pace.
towns.day: You paddle the Loxahatchee River in the morning and snorkel the inlet in the afternoon.

towns.name: Fort Pierce
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: An affordable working waterfront with a big Saturday market.
towns.day: You fish the inlet in the morning and walk the downtown farmers market.
todo: Fishing and beaches at the inlet park.

towns.name: Cocoa Beach
towns.airport: Orlando (MCO), about 50 minutes, or Melbourne (MLB), about 40
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A classic surf town where you can watch rocket launches from the sand.
towns.day: You surf in the morning and watch a launch from the beach in the evening.

towns.name: New Smyrna Beach
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure on the barrier island
towns.blurb: A laid back surf town about an hour from Orlando.
towns.day: You check the surf before breakfast and end the day with tacos on Flagler Avenue.

towns.name: Daytona Beach
towns.watch: Event crowds, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: Wide beaches and some of the most affordable coastal homes in Florida.
towns.day: You drive onto the hard packed beach and set up for the day.
todo: One of the few beaches where you can drive on the sand.

towns.name: Flagler Beach
towns.watch: Beach erosion, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A small, unhurried beach town along A1A, with a new pier on the way.
towns.day: You walk the beach at sunrise and grab lunch on A1A with an ocean view.
todo: Being rebuilt as a longer pier, expected to open in early 2027.

towns.name: St. Augustine
towns.watch: Low lying streets flood in big storms
towns.blurb: The oldest city in the country, with brick streets and beaches a bridge away.
towns.day: You have coffee in the old town before the tour buses arrive and bike over the bridge to the beach.
todo: Colonial streets and the Castillo de San Marcos.

towns.name: Jacksonville Beach
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A lively beach town with surf, patios and a big city next door.
towns.day: You surf by the pier and meet friends for dinner a block from the sand.

towns.name: Fernandina Beach
towns.watch: Storm surge on the island
towns.blurb: A Victorian downtown, shrimp boats and quiet beaches near Georgia.
towns.day: You walk Centre Street for coffee, watch the shrimp boats come in and spend the afternoon on an uncrowded beach.

towns.name: Carrabelle
towns.watch: Storm surge, few services nearby
towns.blurb: A small fishing town on the Forgotten Coast with a working harbor and a slow, friendly pace.
towns.day: You launch at the river before sunrise, run out toward Dog Island and are back at the marina for a late breakfast.
todo: A quiet stretch of Gulf sand just west of town.
cons: Far from big airports and hospitals

towns.name: St. George Island
towns.price: About $1.1M median for the island's zip code, which includes Eastpoint (Redfin, three months ending Aug 2026)
towns.season: Busy summers and spring break, quiet winters
towns.watch: Storm surge on a barrier island. Michael brought at least 5 feet of it in 2018. One bridge on and off
towns.blurb: A barrier island with no high rises, a lighthouse at its center and nine miles of state park beach at the east end.
towns.day: You bike to coffee, spend the day on the state park beach and climb the lighthouse at sunset.
todo: Nine miles of undeveloped beach. Dr. Beach named it number one in America in 2023.
A 77 foot lighthouse with 92 stairs and a small museum, right where the bridge lands.
pros: One of the best beaches in the country
cons: One bridge, and a long drive to an airport or a hospital

towns.name: St. Teresa
towns.aka: Saint Teresa St Teresa Beach SummerCamp Beach
towns.price: Too few sales for a median. Homesites at SummerCamp Beach are marketed from about $62K (St. Joe, Oct 2026)
towns.watch: Storm surge. Hurricane Michael pushed about 12 feet of water into the marine lab next door in 2018. No stores or medical care close by
towns.blurb: A quiet line of beach houses on US 98 east of Carrabelle, beside the FSU Coastal and Marine Lab. There are no stores here, and that is the point.
towns.day: You walk the beach at sunrise, paddle Alligator Harbor before the wind comes up and drive to Carrabelle when the groceries run out.
todo: Free guided tours on Fridays and free evening lectures open to the public.
Two beaches and coastal trails about 20 minutes east.
pros: About as quiet as the Gulf gets
Tallahassee is about an hour away
Wild land and water on every side
cons: No store or restaurant in the community
Few homes come up for sale

towns.name: St. Marks
towns.price: About $219K, based on very few sales (Redfin, three months ending May 2026)
towns.watch: Flooding. Storm surge has put water in town five times since 2005, most recently with Helene in 2024
towns.blurb: A tiny river town where the road ends at the water, half an hour south of Tallahassee, with a Spanish fort site, a rail trail and a huge wildlife refuge next door.
towns.day: You ride the rail trail into town, eat lunch on the river and run the boat four miles down to the bay for the afternoon.
todo: More than 86,000 acres and 43 miles of coast, with a lighthouse rebuilt in 1842.
San Marcos de Apalache Historic State Park
The site of a fort begun in 1679 where the two rivers meet, with a small museum.
Sixteen paved miles of old railroad that end on Riverside Drive.
pros: Half an hour to Tallahassee and its airport
Rivers, a refuge and a rail trail at the door
cons: Floods in nearly every big storm
The nearest supermarket is 16 minutes away

towns.name: Panama City
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure. Parts of town are still rebuilding from Michael in 2018
towns.blurb: A bayfront city on St. Andrews Bay with a reviving downtown and the Gulf beaches a bridge away.
towns.day: You grab coffee downtown, walk the marina in St. Andrews and drive 20 minutes to the beach when you feel like it.
todo: A waterfront district of seafood spots, a marina and a weekend market.
pros: More affordable than the beach side
A year round town, not just a resort

towns.name: Pensacola
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: Florida's westernmost city, with more than 450 years of history, a lively downtown and white sand beaches across the bay.
towns.day: You walk Palafox Street to the Saturday market, catch a Blue Angels practice in season and watch the sunset from the bayfront.
todo: The heart of downtown, lined with restaurants, galleries and a Saturday market.
pros: A real city with history and culture
More affordable than much of the coast
cons: The beaches are a 20 minute drive

towns.name: Pensacola Beach
towns.watch: Barrier island hurricane exposure, bridge traffic in season
towns.blurb: A barrier island town on Santa Rosa Island, with sugar white sand and miles of protected national seashore on both sides.
towns.day: You bike the path along the island at sunrise, spend the day on the sand and walk to the pier for the sunset.
todo: Miles of undeveloped beach and dunes on either side of town.
pros: Stunning beaches with protected land around them

towns.name: Port St. Joe
towns.season: Quiet year round, busier in summer
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure. Michael hit hard here in 2018. The state closed the 2026 scallop season in St. Joseph Bay
towns.blurb: A small town on St. Joseph Bay, known for calm clear water, bay sunsets and the beaches of Cape San Blas.
towns.day: You paddle the clear grass flats in the morning, drive out to Cape San Blas for the beach and watch the sun set over the bay.
todo: A long, quiet peninsula of dunes and beach with a state park at the tip.

towns.name: Crystal River
towns.watch: Storm surge flooding. Hit by recent hurricanes
towns.blurb: A spring fed town on Kings Bay where hundreds of manatees spend the winter.
towns.day: You paddle Kings Bay at first light with manatees surfacing around you, and in summer you head out for scallops.
todo: Clear blue springs and a boardwalk for watching manatees in winter.
cons: Only a small Gulf beach nearby
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Homosassa
towns.watch: Storm surge flooding. Helene flooded Old Homosassa in 2024
towns.blurb: An Old Florida river town known for manatees, scalloping and waterfront spots you can pull up to by boat.
towns.day: You idle down the Homosassa River to the Gulf for scallops and stop at a riverside spot on the way home.
todo: See manatees and native Florida wildlife up close.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Ozello
towns.watch: Very low lying and floods in storms. One winding road in and out
towns.blurb: A handful of homes on marsh islands at the end of a nine mile winding road. About as remote as the Gulf coast gets.
towns.day: You launch a kayak from the back yard, fish the oyster bars and don't see another boat all morning.
todo: A twisting road through salt marsh and hammocks that's a destination by itself.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Steinhatchee
towns.watch: Hit hard by Idalia in 2023 and Helene in 2024. Check rebuilding and flood zones
towns.blurb: A river fishing village on the Big Bend where summer means scallops and the nearest stoplight is a long way off.
towns.day: You run the river to the Gulf at dawn, fill a bucket with scallops and clean them on the dock.
todo: Marinas, fish camps and a straight shot to the grass flats.
cons: Major hurricane damage in recent years
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Apollo Beach
towns.watch: Storm surge on canal homes, commuter traffic on I-75
towns.blurb: A canal community on Tampa Bay where a lot of back yards have a boat lift.
towns.day: You take the boat out through the canals to the bay, and in winter you stop by the manatee viewing center on the way home.
todo: Hundreds of manatees gather in the warm water here on cold days.
pros: Canal front homes at a fair price

towns.name: Clearwater
towns.airport: Tampa (TPA), about 30 minutes, or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE)
towns.watch: Storm surge near the water, beach traffic
towns.blurb: The mainland city behind Clearwater Beach, with a rebuilt downtown waterfront and the sand a bridge away.
towns.day: You catch a concert at Coachman Park on the bluff, then bike the causeway to the beach.
todo: A downtown waterfront park with a big outdoor concert venue.
pros: Near a famous beach without beach prices
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Indian Rocks Beach
towns.airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE) or Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
towns.watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024
towns.blurb: A low key beach town of cottages and small condos, with public beach access at the end of nearly every street.
towns.day: You walk to the beach with a chair, walk home for lunch and walk back for the sunset.
todo: More than two dozen public accesses, many with a little free parking.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Madeira Beach
towns.airport: St. Pete Clearwater (PIE) or Tampa (TPA), about 40 minutes
towns.watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024
towns.blurb: Locals call it Mad Beach: a casual Gulf town built around the fishing boats and boardwalk at John's Pass.
towns.day: You watch the charter boats come in at John's Pass, then cross the street to the beach.
todo: A boardwalk of seafood spots, shops and fishing charters on the inlet.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: New Port Richey
towns.watch: Flooding along the river and coast
towns.blurb: A small river town with a 1920s downtown that has been adding breweries, restaurants and a restored theater.
towns.day: You kayak the Cotee River in the morning and walk Main Street for dinner.
todo: A riverfront park downtown with concerts and events.
cons: Not much of a beach nearby
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Ruskin
towns.watch: Low lying areas flood. Fast growth and traffic
towns.blurb: A fast growing bayside community on the Little Manatee River, with some of the lowest prices near Tampa Bay.
towns.day: You fish the river mouth at sunrise and are home before the day heats up.
todo: A quiet blackwater river for paddling and fishing.

towns.name: Safety Harbor
towns.watch: Bayfront storm surge
towns.blurb: A small town on Old Tampa Bay with oak shaded streets, a historic spa and a Main Street full of local shops.
towns.day: You walk the waterfront park and pier, then have dinner on Main Street without moving the car.
todo: Local restaurants and shops, with a street festival on the third Friday of the month.
pros: A walkable small town close to Tampa
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: St. Pete Beach
towns.airport: Tampa (TPA) or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 35 minutes
towns.watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024
towns.blurb: A wide Gulf beach anchored by the pink Don CeSar hotel, with the old fishing village of Pass-a-Grille at its tip.
towns.day: You have breakfast in Pass-a-Grille, spend the day on the wide Gulf beach and stay for the sunset.
todo: A historic beach village with a sunset bell and no high rises.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: St. Petersburg
towns.airport: Tampa (TPA), about 25 to 35 minutes, or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE)
towns.watch: Flooding in low lying neighborhoods, rising prices
towns.blurb: A sunny waterfront city with a walkable downtown, the Dalí Museum, murals on every block and Gulf beaches 20 minutes away.
towns.day: You walk the waterfront parks to the Pier, wander the Saturday Morning Market and pick a brewery for the afternoon.
todo: A world class collection on the downtown waterfront.
pros: A big arts, food and music scene
A walkable downtown on the water
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Sun City Center
towns.watch: Inland, so there is no beach. Most homes are age restricted to 55 and over
towns.blurb: A golf cart community inland from Tampa Bay with more than 100 clubs. Most homes here are age restricted to 55 and over.
towns.day: You take the golf cart to a morning club meeting, play nine holes and drive it to dinner.
todo: More than 100 clubs and activity groups, from woodworking to pickleball.
pros: A huge calendar of clubs and activities
cons: Age restrictions limit who can buy

towns.name: Tampa
towns.watch: Flooding in low areas (Helene and Milton in 2024), traffic
towns.blurb: The big city of the Gulf coast: a downtown riverwalk, historic Ybor City, pro sports and a major airport.
towns.day: You run the Riverwalk before work, meet friends in Ybor City after and catch a Lightning game downtown.
todo: About 2.6 miles of waterfront path linking parks, museums and restaurants.
pros: Jobs, sports, food and a great airport

towns.name: Tarpon Springs
towns.watch: Flooding near the bayous and river. Helene's surge flooded the Sponge Docks in 2024
towns.blurb: A working sponge port with Greek bakeries and restaurants along the docks and bayous winding through town.
towns.day: You walk the Sponge Docks for coffee and pastry, watch the boats unload and drive to Fred Howard Park for the sunset.
todo: Sponge boats, restaurants and bakeries along Dodecanese Boulevard.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Treasure Island
towns.airport: Tampa (TPA) or St. Pete Clearwater (PIE), about 35 minutes
towns.watch: Barrier island flooding. Hit by Helene in 2024
towns.blurb: A barrier island with one of the widest beaches on the Gulf.
towns.day: You cross a long stretch of sand to reach the water, and on Sundays you stay for the drum circle at sunset.
todo: A paved walkway about a mile long, running along the dunes.
pros: A huge beach that never feels crowded
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Bradenton
towns.watch: Flooding along the river
towns.blurb: A river city with a long Riverwalk, spring training baseball and the Anna Maria Island beaches 20 minutes west.
towns.day: You walk the Riverwalk in the morning, catch a Pirates spring training game and head to the island for sunset.
todo: A neighborhood of colorful cottages turned into galleries and cafes.
pros: Affordable for this stretch of coast

towns.name: Bradenton Beach
towns.watch: Island flooding. Hit hard by Helene in 2024. Cortez Bridge replacement work is planned through about 2029
towns.blurb: The south end of Anna Maria Island, with a historic fishing pier, a walkable Bridge Street and water on both sides.
towns.day: You walk Bridge Street to the pier for breakfast and cross the road to the Gulf for the rest of the day.
todo: A short, walkable strip of restaurants and shops that ends at the pier.
pros: Walk to the beach, the bay and dinner

towns.name: Cortez
towns.watch: Low lying, with storm surge risk. The Cortez Bridge is set to be replaced, with work running to about 2029
towns.blurb: One of the last working fishing villages in Florida, with fish houses on the bay that date back to the 1880s.
towns.day: You eat lunch at a fish house on the water and watch the boats come in.
todo: A February weekend of seafood, music and boat tours.
cons: Tiny, with few homes for sale

towns.name: Englewood
towns.watch: Storm surge. Hit by Ian in 2022 and by Helene and Milton in 2024
towns.blurb: A laid back Gulf town with a small old downtown and beaches on Manasota Key, known for shark teeth.
towns.day: You walk Stump Pass Beach looking for shark teeth, then head to Dearborn Street for the farmers market.
todo: A mile of undeveloped beach at the tip of Manasota Key.

towns.name: Sarasota
towns.aka: Sarasota Beach Lido Key Lido Beach St Armands Circle
towns.watch: Storm surge (Helene and Milton in 2024), season traffic
towns.blurb: The arts capital of the Gulf coast, with an opera, a ballet, The Ringling museum, Lido Beach just over the bridge and Siesta Key's famous sand minutes away.
towns.day: You walk the bayfront at sunrise, spend the afternoon at The Ringling and see a show downtown at night.
todo: An art museum, a circus museum and a bayfront mansion on 66 acres.
A walkable circle of shops and restaurants on Lido Key, a few blocks from Lido Beach.
pros: Arts and dining well beyond its size
St. Armands Circle and Lido Beach are just over the bridge
cons: Bridge traffic to the beach in season

towns.name: Siesta Key
towns.watch: Bridge traffic, storm surge
towns.blurb: An island of quartz white sand so fine it stays cool underfoot, with a small, lively village at the north end.
towns.day: You walk to Siesta Beach before the crowds, have lunch in the Village and come back for the Sunday drum circle.
todo: Named the number one beach in America by Tripadvisor in 2025.
pros: One of the best beaches anywhere

towns.name: Venice
towns.price: $384K median on the mainland, $550K on the island
towns.watch: Storm surge on the island and near the water
towns.blurb: A 1920s planned town of palm lined avenues you can walk from downtown to the Gulf, with newer mainland neighborhoods and the Legacy Trail just over the bridge.
towns.day: You hunt for shark teeth on the beach, walk Venice Avenue for lunch and watch the sunset from the jetty.
todo: A palm lined main street of shops and restaurants that ends at the beach.
A paved rail trail of about 18 miles running north to Sarasota.
pros: Walkable from downtown to the beach
More home for the money on the mainland side
cons: The island costs more than the mainland
From mainland neighborhoods you drive to the beach

towns.name: Bonita Springs
towns.aka: Bonita Beach Little Hickory Island Lovers Key
towns.watch: Season traffic on US 41, flood zones west of 41, storm surge at the beach. County beach parking lots were closed for repairs in fall 2026
towns.blurb: A city between Naples and Fort Myers with a small historic downtown, golf communities and a quiet Gulf beach on Little Hickory Island, next to Lovers Key.
towns.day: You play a morning round, have lunch downtown by the river and catch the sunset at Bonita Beach.
todo: A downtown park on the Imperial River with concerts and art festivals.
Two miles of beach, plus trails and kayak routes through the mangroves.
pros: Close to both Naples and the airport
cons: Mostly gated communities, so you drive everywhere
The beach was hit hard by Hurricane Ian
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Cape Coral
towns.watch: Storm surge (Ian in 2022) and insurance costs. Not every canal reaches the Gulf
towns.blurb: A city of more than 400 miles of canals, where a boat in the back yard is normal and waterfront is still within reach.
towns.day: You lower the boat off the lift, idle out the canal to the river and are fishing the Gulf within the hour.
todo: A marina village with waterfront dining, live music and boat watching.
pros: Waterfront homes at lower prices than most of the coast
cons: No real Gulf beach in town
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Chokoloskee
towns.season: Quiet. Winter is prime fishing season
towns.watch: Very low lying and isolated, with storm surge risk
towns.blurb: A tiny shell mound island at the edge of Everglades National Park, the last stop before the Ten Thousand Islands.
towns.day: You pole a skiff through the mangrove islands for snook and stop at the old Smallwood Store on the way in.
todo: A maze of mangrove islands for fishing, paddling and camping.
towns.area_name: Naples, Marco Island and the Everglades

towns.name: Everglades City
towns.price: Thin data. About $250K to $400K depending on the source (Redfin and Zillow, late 2025 to 2026)
towns.season: Busy November through April, very quiet in summer
towns.watch: Storm surge. Wilma in 2005, Irma in 2017 and Ian in 2022 all flooded town, and nearly every property is in a flood zone
towns.blurb: A small fishing town on the Barron River at the edge of Everglades National Park, known for stone crab and as the way into the Ten Thousand Islands.
towns.day: You launch a kayak at the national park visitor center, eat stone crab on the river for lunch and catch the Third Thursday talk at the museum.
todo: The new Marjory Stoneman Douglas Visitor Center opened in December 2025, with boat tours and a kayak launch.
The county's history museum, a short walk from the circle. Open Tuesday through Saturday.
A maze of mangrove islands for fishing, paddling and camping, starting right off the dock.
pros: Wild Florida and big water at the door
A real small town with a busy calendar in season
Lower prices than Naples or Marco Island
cons: Storm surge has flooded town again and again
Supermarket, pharmacy and hospital are 35 to 45 minutes away
Very quiet and very hot in summer
towns.area_name: Naples, Marco Island and the Everglades

towns.name: Fort Myers
towns.watch: Flooding along the river. Hit by Ian in 2022
towns.blurb: The City of Palms, with a brick street River District downtown and the winter homes of Edison and Ford on the river.
towns.day: You tour the Edison and Ford estates, walk First Street for dinner and catch live music in the River District.
todo: Brick streets, restaurants and monthly art and music walks downtown.
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Fort Myers Beach
towns.watch: Still rebuilding after Hurricane Ian in 2022. Check flood zones and construction nearby
towns.blurb: Seven miles of soft sand on Estero Island, rebuilding after Hurricane Ian with its beach town spirit intact.
towns.day: You walk the beach at low tide, have lunch near Times Square and watch the shrimp boats head out at dusk.
todo: The pedestrian plaza at the center of the island's rebuilding. A new pier is under construction.
cons: Major storm damage and ongoing construction
One road on and off the island
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Marco Island
towns.watch: Storm surge, high insurance
towns.blurb: The largest of the Ten Thousand Islands, with a wide crescent beach on one side and wild mangrove country on the other.
towns.day: You shell on Tigertail Beach at low tide, then take the boat into the Ten Thousand Islands for the afternoon.
todo: A lagoon and sandbar beach known for shelling and shorebirds.
towns.area_name: Naples, Marco Island and the Everglades

towns.name: Port Charlotte
towns.watch: Storm damage history (Charley in 2004, Ian in 2022), flood zones
towns.blurb: A canal community on Charlotte Harbor with some of the most affordable waterfront homes in Southwest Florida.
towns.day: You run the canals out to the harbor for tarpon and snook, then catch a spring training game at the ballpark.
todo: One of the best tarpon and snook fisheries in the state.
cons: Car dependent, with a spread out layout
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Punta Gorda
towns.watch: Storm surge. Hit by Ian in 2022, and downtown flooded again in 2024
towns.blurb: A small harbor town with brick streets, a waterfront Harborwalk and sailboat canals that lead to the Gulf.
towns.day: You bike the Harborwalk, have lunch at Fishermen's Village and sail the harbor before sunset.
todo: A waterfront path linking parks, the marina and Fishermen's Village.
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Sanibel Island
towns.watch: Hit hard by Hurricane Ian in 2022 and mostly rebuilt. Check flood zones. The causeway is the only road
towns.blurb: A barrier island famous for shells, with 25 miles of bike paths, no traffic lights and more than half the island preserved.
towns.day: You do the Sanibel stoop for shells at sunrise, bike to the Ding Darling refuge and ride home for the sunset.
todo: J.N. Ding Darling National Wildlife Refuge
Thousands of acres of mangroves and wading birds.
pros: Nature comes first, with strict building limits
towns.area_name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor

towns.name: Key Largo
towns.watch: A long evacuation drive, high insurance
towns.blurb: The first Key off the mainland and the dive capital of the country, with a coral reef state park offshore.
towns.day: You're on a dive boat to the reef by 8, back for fish tacos by the water at noon and in a hammock by 2.
todo: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
The first undersea park in the country, for snorkeling, diving and glass bottom boats.

towns.name: Bal Harbour
towns.airport: Miami (MIA) or Fort Lauderdale (FLL), about 35 minutes
towns.watch: Very high prices, flooding, traffic
towns.blurb: A tiny oceanfront village at the north tip of Miami Beach, known for a luxury shopping center and a quiet beach path.
towns.day: You jog the beach path at sunrise, have a long lunch at the Bal Harbour Shops and walk the beach at dusk.
todo: An open air luxury mall with palm lined courtyards.
cons: Among the priciest places in Florida

towns.name: Boca Raton
towns.airport: Palm Beach airport or Fort Lauderdale (FLL), about 30 minutes
towns.watch: Traffic, higher insurance
towns.blurb: A polished city of pink Mediterranean buildings, big parks and beaches kept natural behind a line of dunes.
towns.day: You walk the boardwalk at Gumbo Limbo, have lunch at Mizner Park and catch an outdoor concert at the amphitheater.
todo: A walkable plaza of shops, restaurants, an art museum and an amphitheater.

towns.name: Dania Beach
towns.watch: Airport noise, flooding
towns.blurb: A small, unflashy beach city right next to the Fort Lauderdale airport, with a fishing pier and a quiet beach.
towns.day: You fish off the pier at sunrise, have lunch at a dockside spot and can be at your gate 15 minutes after leaving home.
todo: A long fishing pier with a restaurant at the foot.
cons: Fewer restaurants and shops in town

towns.name: Hallandale Beach
towns.watch: Traffic, flooding, condo fees and assessments
towns.blurb: A city of oceanfront condo towers between Fort Lauderdale and Miami, home to Gulfstream Park.
towns.day: You walk the beach in the morning, watch the horses run at Gulfstream Park and stay for dinner in the village there.
todo: Horse racing, a casino and an outdoor village of shops and restaurants.
pros: Condos at lower prices than Miami Beach
cons: Not much of a walkable center

towns.name: Highland Beach
towns.watch: Oceanfront storm exposure, high condo fees
towns.blurb: A three mile strip of oceanfront condos and homes between Boca Raton and Delray Beach, with no shops and no crowds.
towns.day: You walk a beach with almost nobody on it, then drive ten minutes to Atlantic Avenue when you want company.
todo: Quiet, mostly residential sand. There is no public beach access or parking in town today.
cons: Nothing in town to walk to

towns.name: Hollywood
towns.watch: Flooding in low areas, traffic
towns.blurb: A beach city with a 2.5 mile oceanfront Broadwalk for walking and biking, plus a downtown full of murals.
towns.day: You bike the Broadwalk before it gets hot, stop for breakfast a few steps from the sand and catch a concert at the bandshell.
todo: A 2.5 mile brick promenade along the ocean, lined with cafes.
pros: The Broadwalk makes beach life car free

towns.name: Lauderdale by the Sea
towns.watch: Oceanfront storm exposure
towns.blurb: A low rise beach village where a coral reef sits close enough to shore that you can snorkel it from the sand.
towns.day: You snorkel the reef off the beach in the morning, walk to lunch in the square and listen to live music there at night.
todo: The little downtown by the pier, with restaurants and outdoor music.

towns.name: Lighthouse Point
towns.watch: Canal flooding at king tides, high prices
towns.blurb: A boating town of deep water canals near Hillsboro Inlet, where most streets end at the water.
towns.day: You run the boat out Hillsboro Inlet for mahi and tie up at a waterfront restaurant on the way home.
todo: A quick route to the ocean, watched over by a historic lighthouse.

towns.name: North Miami Beach
towns.airport: Miami (MIA) or Fort Lauderdale (FLL), about 30 minutes
towns.watch: Traffic. Despite the name, it is not on the ocean
towns.blurb: A mainland city in north Miami-Dade with restaurants from all over the world and Oleta River State Park next door.
towns.day: You mountain bike or paddle at Oleta River State Park, then pick from a dozen cuisines for dinner.
todo: The largest urban park in Florida, with trails, kayaking and a small beach.
pros: More affordable than the beach towns
cons: The ocean is a drive over the causeway

towns.name: North Palm Beach
towns.watch: Storm surge on the waterfront
towns.blurb: A village wrapped in water, between the Intracoastal and Lake Worth, with a state park beach across the bridge.
towns.day: You paddle to Munyon Island in the morning and play the village golf course in the afternoon.
todo: John D. MacArthur Beach State Park
A natural barrier island beach reached by a long boardwalk.

towns.name: Palm Beach
towns.watch: Extremely high prices, road closures and traffic at times
towns.blurb: A barrier island of clipped hedges, grand estates and Worth Avenue, with a bike trail along the lake.
towns.day: You ride the Lake Trail past the estates, walk the little courtyards off Worth Avenue and have dinner somewhere that's been there for decades.
todo: A paved path along the Intracoastal for walking and biking.
cons: One of the most expensive towns in the country

towns.name: Palm Beach Gardens
towns.watch: Inland, so the beach is a drive. HOA rules are common
towns.blurb: A green, golf centered city a few miles inland, home to PGA National and a lot of shopping and dining.
towns.day: You play 18 in the morning, meet friends for dinner near the Gardens Mall and drive ten minutes to the beach on Sunday.
todo: A resort with several championship golf courses.
pros: Golf, shopping and dining close by

towns.name: Riviera Beach
towns.watch: Storm exposure on Singer Island. The mainland and the island are very different markets
towns.blurb: A working port city with a big public marina, Peanut Island offshore and the beaches of Singer Island across the bridge.
towns.day: You take the water taxi to Peanut Island to snorkel, then cross to Singer Island for the beach.
todo: A small island park in the inlet with clear water for snorkeling.
pros: Great boating with a quick inlet
cons: The mainland and the island feel very different

towns.name: Sunny Isles Beach
towns.airport: Fort Lauderdale (FLL) or Miami (MIA), about 30 minutes
towns.watch: Traffic on Collins Avenue, high condo fees
towns.blurb: A two mile line of luxury condo towers on the ocean between Miami Beach and Fort Lauderdale.
towns.day: You take the elevator down to the beach, walk to the pier for lunch and watch the lights come on from your balcony.
todo: A historic pier with a restaurant over the water.
pros: Ocean views from nearly every home

towns.name: West Palm Beach
towns.watch: Traffic, rising prices
towns.blurb: The downtown of Palm Beach County, with Clematis Street, a waterfront, the Norton Museum of Art and a Brightline train station.
towns.day: You walk the waterfront to the Saturday GreenMarket, spend the afternoon at the Norton and stay out on Clematis Street.
todo: The main downtown strip for restaurants, bars and live music.
pros: A real downtown with nightlife and arts
The airport and the train are minutes away
cons: The ocean beach is across the bridge in Palm Beach

towns.name: Wilton Manors
towns.watch: Flooding at king tides, traffic
towns.blurb: A small island city ringed by the Middle River, built around the restaurants, bars and shops of Wilton Drive.
towns.day: You kayak the river loop around the city in the morning and walk Wilton Drive for dinner and a show at night.
todo: A walkable main street of restaurants, bars and shops.

towns.name: Jensen Beach
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure, lagoon water quality
towns.blurb: A small, colorful river town with a Caribbean streak and uncrowded Hutchinson Island beaches across the causeway.
towns.day: You paddle the Indian River Lagoon in the morning and walk downtown for dinner and live music.
todo: A few blocks of local restaurants and shops by the river.

towns.name: Port St. Lucie
towns.watch: Fast growth and traffic. Inland from the beach
towns.blurb: One of the fastest growing cities in Florida: newer homes, golf, Mets spring training and beaches 20 minutes east.
towns.day: You paddle the North Fork of the St. Lucie River, catch a Mets game in March and drive out to the beach on weekends.
todo: A planned town center with shops, restaurants and community events.
cons: Spread out, with no real downtown

towns.name: Sebastian
towns.airport: Melbourne (MLB), about 35 minutes, or Vero Beach, about 25
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure, few big city services
towns.blurb: A riverfront fishing town on the Indian River Lagoon, near the country's first wildlife refuge and a famous surf inlet.
towns.day: You fish the lagoon at sunrise, have lunch on the riverfront and watch the surfers at Sebastian Inlet.
todo: Top surfing and fishing on both sides of the inlet. Bridge work started in 2026, so check access first.

towns.name: Stuart
towns.watch: River water quality after Lake Okeechobee releases, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: The Sailfish Capital of the World, with a small historic downtown and a riverwalk on the St. Lucie River.
towns.day: You're offshore for sailfish at dawn, back downtown for lunch on the riverwalk and at the Sunday green market downtown.
todo: A compact historic district of shops, restaurants and a riverwalk stage.
cons: River water quality problems some summers

towns.name: Vero Beach
towns.airport: Melbourne (MLB), about 45 minutes. Vero's own airport has a few airline flights
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A quietly polished town with strict height limits, an oceanside village of shops and a serious arts scene.
towns.day: You walk the beach at Humiston Park, browse Ocean Drive and see a play at Riverside Theatre.
todo: A professional theater next to the Vero Beach Museum of Art.
pros: No high rises on the beach
Strong arts for a small town

towns.name: Indialantic
towns.watch: Barrier island hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A small oceanside town with a boardwalk, a couple of surf shops and rocket launches you can watch from the sand.
towns.day: You surf before breakfast, walk Fifth Avenue for a taco and watch a launch light up the sky after dinner.
todo: A short oceanfront boardwalk with easy beach access.

towns.name: Melbourne Beach
towns.watch: Barrier island hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: One of the oldest beach towns on the Space Coast, a few quiet streets between the ocean and the Indian River.
towns.day: You walk the historic pier on the river at sunrise, and in summer you can book a guided night walk to see sea turtles nest.
todo: One of the most important sea turtle nesting beaches in the world.

towns.name: Palm Bay
towns.watch: Spread out, and not on the ocean
towns.blurb: The biggest city on the Space Coast, with lots of land, newer homes and some of the lowest prices near the beach.
towns.day: You hike Turkey Creek Sanctuary in the morning and drive 20 minutes to the beach in the afternoon.
todo: Boardwalks and trails along a quiet creek.
pros: Close to aerospace and tech jobs
cons: No downtown or beach of its own

towns.name: Satellite Beach
towns.watch: Beach erosion, hurricane exposure. Beach parking is paid year round
towns.blurb: A residential beach town between the ocean and the Banana River, with surf breaks, parks and front row launch views.
towns.day: You surf at sunrise, hit the skate park or the dog park and watch a rocket go up from your street.
todo: A beachfront park with pavilions and a dune crossover.
cons: A narrow, eroding beach in spots

towns.name: Titusville
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure, lagoon water quality
towns.blurb: The town across the river from the launch pads, with the best rocket views anywhere and a huge wildlife refuge next door.
towns.day: You bike the trail downtown, watch a launch from the riverfront and drive the wildlife loop at Merritt Island at dusk.
todo: 140,000 acres of marsh and scrub next to Canaveral National Seashore.
pros: Launches and wild beaches close by
cons: The beach is a 20 minute drive

towns.name: West Melbourne
towns.watch: Inland, with traffic on the main roads
towns.blurb: A fast growing inland city with newer neighborhoods and big box shopping, 20 minutes from the beach.
towns.day: You run errands in ten minutes flat and save the beach for the weekend.
todo: An accessible sports park and community gathering spot.

towns.name: Atlantic Beach
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure, rising prices
towns.blurb: A leafy beach town with a walkable town center it shares with Neptune Beach, and the trails of Hanna Park to the north.
towns.day: You surf or walk the beach at sunrise, bike to Beaches Town Center for coffee and ride the trails at Hanna Park.
todo: A few walkable blocks of restaurants and shops at the ocean.
pros: A walkable center by the beach

towns.name: Neptune Beach
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A small residential beach town that shares a walkable town center with Atlantic Beach.
towns.day: You walk to the beach with a board, then walk to Beaches Town Center for dinner.
todo: Restaurants, a bookstore and shops a block from the sand.

towns.name: Ponte Vedra Beach
towns.season: Busy during The Players in March
towns.watch: Limited public beach access, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A golf town on the ocean, home to TPC Sawgrass and The Players Championship, with tall dunes and a huge coastal preserve.
towns.day: You play the Stadium Course, or at least watch someone hit the island green, then walk the dunes at Guana.
todo: Miles of trails, marsh and undeveloped beach.
cons: Little public beach parking and no real downtown

towns.name: St. Augustine Beach
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure, erosion
towns.blurb: A relaxed beach town on Anastasia Island, ten minutes from the oldest city in the country.
towns.day: You walk the wide beach, stop by the farmers market at the pier park when it's on and head into old St. Augustine for dinner.
todo: Four miles of protected beach, plus a tidal lagoon for paddling.
pros: Easygoing beach life with history next door
cons: An hour to a major airport

towns.name: Daytona Beach Shores
towns.watch: Condo assessments, event traffic, hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: A quiet strip of oceanfront condos just south of Daytona Beach, with the river a block behind you.
towns.day: You walk out of the lobby onto the sand, and drive up to Daytona only when you want the noise.
todo: A lighthouse you can climb and a marine science center, ten minutes south.
cons: Not much in town besides the beach

towns.name: Ormond Beach
towns.watch: Hurricane exposure
towns.blurb: Daytona's quieter neighbor to the north, with oak canopy roads, a small downtown and the same hard packed beach.
towns.day: You drive the Ormond Scenic Loop under the oaks, walk the beach and have dinner on Granada Boulevard.
todo: About 30 miles of canopy road, marsh and ocean views.
pros: Quieter than Daytona, with more green space

towns.name: Palm Coast
towns.watch: Canal homes can flood in storms. Car dependent
towns.blurb: A planned city of saltwater canals and more than 130 miles of trails, between St. Augustine and Daytona.
towns.day: You bike the trails under the oaks, take the boat down the canal to the Intracoastal and drive ten minutes to the beach.
todo: Formal gardens on one side of A1A and a beach of coquina rock on the other.
pros: Canal homes and trails at fair prices

towns.name: Port Orange
towns.watch: Hurricane and river flooding
towns.blurb: A suburb on the Halifax River just south of Daytona, with parks, a riverfront and the beach over the bridge.
towns.day: You paddle Spruce Creek in the morning and cross the Dunlawton Bridge to the beach in the afternoon.
todo: Trails and a blackwater creek for paddling.
pros: Close to the beach and the airport
cons: Suburban, without much of a downtown

towns.name: South Daytona
towns.watch: River flooding, event traffic
towns.blurb: A small riverfront city tucked between Daytona Beach and Port Orange, with low prices and the beach ten minutes away.
towns.day: You walk the riverfront park at sunrise and are on the beach before your coffee gets cold.
todo: A park and boardwalk on the Halifax River.
pros: Among the most affordable spots near the ocean

towns.name: Mexico Beach
towns.watch: Storm exposure; rebuilding and new homes sit alongside older beach cottages.
towns.blurb: A low-rise Gulf beach town with pastel cottages, public white-sand beaches and a fishing canal at its west end.
towns.day: Walk to the beach, launch a fishing boat from the canal, and return for sunset.

towns.name: Perdido Key
towns.blurb: Quiet barrier-island beaches, white condos and protected dunes.

towns.name: Gulf Breeze
towns.blurb: Leafy bayside neighborhoods between Pensacola Bay and Santa Rosa Sound.

towns.name: Navarre
towns.blurb: Soundside neighborhoods and boating beside the bridge to Navarre Beach.

towns.name: Navarre Beach
towns.blurb: White sand, a long Gulf fishing pier, pastel beach homes and condo towers.

towns.name: Fort Walton Beach
towns.blurb: A walkable low downtown on Santa Rosa Sound with waterfront parks and Brooks Bridge.

towns.name: Okaloosa Island
towns.blurb: Beachfront resort blocks, white sand and the fishing pier across the sound from downtown.

towns.name: Mary Esther
towns.blurb: Low residential streets beneath coastal tree cover beside Santa Rosa Sound.

towns.name: Shalimar
towns.blurb: Small bayou neighborhoods with marinas, sheltered water and leafy streets.

towns.name: Niceville
towns.blurb: Boggy Bayou, working docks and oak-shaded neighborhoods on Choctawhatchee Bay.

towns.name: Valparaiso
towns.blurb: Low historic homes and waterfront parks along Boggy Bayou.

towns.name: Miramar Beach
towns.blurb: Gulf condos and pastel beach neighborhoods alongside the white-sand shore.

towns.name: Freeport
towns.blurb: A small bayhead town of creeks, boat ramps and wooded neighborhoods.

towns.name: Keaton Beach
towns.blurb: Raised fishing cottages, canals, a public boat ramp and broad salt marsh.

towns.name: Horseshoe Beach
towns.blurb: A working Gulf fishing village of stilt homes, canals and boat basins, rather than a sandy beach.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Suwannee
towns.blurb: Fishing camps and canal homes where the Suwannee River meets marsh islands and the Gulf.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Yankeetown
towns.blurb: Painted cottages beneath live oaks along the Withlacoochee River.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Inglis
towns.blurb: A low river town with wooded lots and access to the Withlacoochee and Gulf.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Hernando Beach
towns.blurb: Canal neighborhoods, marinas and waterfront restaurants beside open Gulf marsh.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Weeki Wachee
towns.blurb: Spring-fed river, wooded neighborhoods and small waterfront homes along the river toward the Gulf.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Aripeka
towns.blurb: A small fishing settlement of old cottages, creek bridges and salt marsh.
towns.area_name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend

towns.name: Oldsmar
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: Low wooded neighborhoods and a walkable small center beside the parks and tidal shoreline of upper Tampa Bay.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Palm Harbor
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: Historic porch homes around Florida Avenue, oak-shaded residential streets and the sheltered waterfront of Ozona and Crystal Beach.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Belleair Beach
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: A quiet residential barrier island of Gulf homes, low beach condos and Intracoastal docks.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Indian Shores
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: A narrow Gulf Boulevard beach town of pastel condominiums, small motels and the Intracoastal Waterway.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Redington Shores
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: White and pastel Gulf condos with low cottages and canal-front homes behind Gulf Boulevard.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: North Redington Beach
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: A compact beach resort strip with white condos, small hotels and sheltered residential waterfront streets.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Redington Beach
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: Low residential beach streets and waterfront homes between the Gulf sand and Boca Ciega Bay.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Tierra Verde
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: Island canal homes, marinas and low condominiums along the Pinellas Bayway toward Fort De Soto.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Holiday
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: Low bungalow neighborhoods and lake streets giving way to mangroves, tidal creeks and Gulf waterfront parks.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Port Richey
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: A working river-mouth waterfront of fishing docks, marinas and low homes where the Pithlachascotee meets the Gulf.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Hudson
towns.region: Gulf Coast · St. Pete and Clearwater
towns.blurb: Hudson Beach, canal neighborhoods and working marinas beside broad Gulf marsh.
towns.area_name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches

towns.name: Gibsonton
towns.blurb: Low riverfront homes, boat ramps and working yards along the Alafia River and eastern Tampa Bay.

towns.name: Boynton Beach
towns.blurb: Lagoon marinas, a working inlet and low coastal neighborhoods.

towns.name: Lake Worth Beach
towns.blurb: Colorful historic cottages and a walkable downtown between the lagoon and ocean beach.

towns.name: Juno Beach
towns.blurb: Oceanfront condos, sea-turtle beaches and the long fishing pier.

towns.name: Tequesta
towns.blurb: Leafy river neighborhoods and boating around the Loxahatchee and Jupiter Inlet.

towns.name: Lantana
towns.blurb: An older fishing-town waterfront with low cottages along the lagoon.

towns.name: Lake Park
towns.blurb: Low-rise neighborhoods and a marina on Lake Worth Lagoon, with new waterfront towers.

towns.name: Palm Beach Shores
towns.blurb: Compact island streets between the inlet, marinas and Atlantic beach.

regions.name: Pensacola and the Emerald Coast
regions.text: The western Panhandle runs from historic Pensacola east to Panama City Beach. In between are Destin's harbor and the small beach towns of 30A, all on sugar white sand and clear green water.

regions.name: The Forgotten Coast
regions.text: East of Panama City the high rises stop. Port St. Joe, Apalachicola and Carrabelle are small working waterfront towns on quiet bays, St. George Island has the long empty beaches, and the coast runs on east past St. Teresa to the river town of St. Marks, half an hour from Tallahassee.

regions.name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend
regions.text: Where the Panhandle bends into the peninsula, the coast turns to marsh and there is very little development. Life here is springs, rivers, scalloping and fishing, in towns like Cedar Key, Crystal River and Steinhatchee.

regions.name: Tampa Bay
regions.text: Tampa Bay, the Pinellas beaches, Anna Maria Island, Bradenton and Sarasota, south through Siesta Key.

regions.name: Southwest Florida Coast
regions.text: Venice and Englewood through Charlotte Harbor, Fort Myers, Sanibel and Captiva, south to Naples, Marco Island, Everglades City and Chokoloskee.

regions.name: The Florida Keys
regions.text: A chain of islands strung along one highway for more than 100 miles, from Key Largo to Key West. Everything here revolves around the water: diving, fishing, sailing and sunsets.

regions.name: Miami and Fort Lauderdale
regions.text: The most urban stretch of the Florida coast, from the Art Deco blocks of South Beach north through Hollywood to the canals of Fort Lauderdale. Two major airports, late nights and beaches with a city right behind them.

regions.name: The Palm Beaches
regions.text: From Boca Raton up to Jupiter, this stretch mixes lively downtowns in Delray Beach and West Palm Beach with quiet oceanfront towns, golf communities and clear water at the inlets.

regions.name: The Treasure Coast
regions.text: Named for the Spanish treasure fleet that wrecked here in 1715. It is a lower key run of river towns and uncrowded barrier island beaches from Stuart to Sebastian, with no high rise skyline.

regions.name: The Space Coast
regions.text: The coast around Cape Canaveral, where rocket launches are part of the view. Surf towns line the barrier island, and the mainland cities have some of the lowest prices near the Atlantic.

regions.name: Daytona, New Smyrna and Flagler
regions.text: Wide, hard packed beaches run from New Smyrna Beach up through Daytona to Flagler Beach. Surf towns, race week crowds and some of the most affordable oceanfront in Florida share this stretch.

regions.name: The First Coast
regions.text: Northeast Florida, from the brick streets of St. Augustine to Fernandina Beach on Amelia Island. Expect wide beaches, real seasons and the Jacksonville beach towns in between.

sourceRegions.name: Pensacola and the Emerald Coast
sourceRegions.text: The western Panhandle runs from historic Pensacola east to Panama City Beach. In between are Destin's harbor and the small beach towns of 30A, all on sugar white sand and clear green water.

sourceRegions.name: The Forgotten Coast
sourceRegions.text: East of Panama City the high rises stop. Port St. Joe, Apalachicola and Carrabelle are small working waterfront towns on quiet bays, St. George Island has the long empty beaches, and the coast runs on east past St. Teresa to the river town of St. Marks, half an hour from Tallahassee.

sourceRegions.name: The Nature Coast and Big Bend
sourceRegions.text: Where the Panhandle bends into the peninsula, the coast turns to marsh and there is very little development. Life here is springs, rivers, scalloping and fishing, in towns like Cedar Key, Crystal River and Steinhatchee.

sourceRegions.name: St. Pete and the Clearwater Beaches
sourceRegions.text: A narrow peninsula between the Gulf and Tampa Bay that packs in a walkable waterfront city, a string of barrier island beach towns and a few small bayside downtowns. Tampa's airport is close to all of it.

sourceRegions.name: Tampa and the South Shore
sourceRegions.text: The east side of Tampa Bay is the big city and the canal communities south of it. You trade Gulf beaches for jobs, pro sports, a major airport and boating on the bay.

sourceRegions.name: Sarasota, Bradenton and Venice
sourceRegions.text: From the Manatee River down to Englewood, this stretch pairs an arts minded city with some of the Gulf's best known sand on Anna Maria Island, Longboat Key and Siesta Key. Venice adds a walkable island downtown.

sourceRegions.name: Fort Myers, Sanibel and Charlotte Harbor
sourceRegions.text: Charlotte Harbor, the Caloosahatchee River and the barrier islands of Sanibel and Captiva make this boating and shelling country. Much of it was hit hard by Hurricane Ian in 2022 and has been rebuilding since.

sourceRegions.name: Naples, Marco Island and the Everglades
sourceRegions.text: The polished southwest corner of the state, with calm Gulf beaches, golf and a walkable downtown in Naples. Past Marco Island the road ends at Everglades City and Chokoloskee, on the edge of the Ten Thousand Islands and Everglades National Park.
